rules.explain_en: When a third tone comes right before another third tone, the first one is said as a second tone: 水果 is written ㄕㄨㄟˇ ㄍㄨㄛˇ and said ㄕㄨㄟˊ ㄍㄨㄛˇ. In Taiwan this happens every time. This change is never written: the MOE dictionary writes the base tone. Turn on “show sandhi” to see the tone you say.
rules.explain_zh: 兩個三聲連在一起時，前面的三聲要唸成二聲：水果寫作ㄕㄨㄟˇ ㄍㄨㄛˇ，唸成ㄕㄨㄟˊ ㄍㄨㄛˇ。在臺灣每次都這樣唸。這個變調從來不標出來，教育部辭典寫的是本調。打開「顯示變調」就能看到實際的唸法。

rules.explain_en: Before a first, second or fourth tone, or a neutral tone, a third tone is a low 21 with no rise, like 老 in 老師. In Taiwan the third tone is usually low and the final rise is rare, so the app teaches it as low (21): let it rise only when the syllable is said on its own or ends a phrase. The spelling does not change.
rules.explain_zh: 三聲後面接一聲、二聲、四聲或輕聲時，只唸成低的21，不往上揚，例如老師的「老」。臺灣的三聲通常是低調，很少上揚，所以這裡教低的21：只有單獨唸或在一個片語（一小段話）的最後才可以上揚。寫法不變。

rules.explain_en: 一 is written ㄧ. As a number or an ordinal it stays ㄧ (第一, 十一). Before a fourth tone it becomes ㄧˊ (一定). Before a first, second or third tone it becomes ㄧˋ (一天, 一起). 一個 is written ㄧ ˙ㄍㄜ: 個 is neutral here, but on its own it is ㄍㄜˋ, a fourth tone, so 一 follows the fourth-tone rule and is said ㄧˊ. The MOE dictionary writes the base tone ㄧ; school textbooks often print the changed tone. Turn on “show sandhi” to see the tone you say. 七 and 八 before a fourth tone can change too, but that is old-fashioned and optional, so it is not drilled.
rules.explain_zh: 「一」寫作ㄧ。當數字或序數時不變（第一、十一）；在四聲前面變成ㄧˊ（一定）；在一聲、二聲、三聲前面變成ㄧˋ（一天、一起）。「一個」寫作ㄧ ˙ㄍㄜ：「個」在這裡唸輕聲，但它本來是四聲ㄍㄜˋ，所以「一」照四聲前面的規則唸成ㄧˊ。教育部辭典寫本調ㄧ，學校課本常直接印出變調。打開「顯示變調」就能看到實際的唸法。「七」、「八」在四聲前面也可以變調，但這是比較舊、可唸可不唸的說法，這裡不練習。

rules.explain_en: 不 is written ㄅㄨˋ. Before a fourth tone it becomes ㄅㄨˊ (不要, 不是). Before other tones it stays ㄅㄨˋ (不好, 不能). The MOE dictionary writes the base tone ㄅㄨˋ; school textbooks often print the changed tone. Turn on “show sandhi” to see the tone you say.
rules.explain_zh: 「不」寫作ㄅㄨˋ。在四聲前面變成ㄅㄨˊ（不要、不是）；在其他聲調前面不變（不好、不能）。教育部辭典寫本調ㄅㄨˋ，學校課本常直接印出變調。打開「顯示變調」就能看到實際的唸法。
